HIGHLIGHTS 
 
PHOTO EXPERIENCE LTD. NAMED OFFALY 
ENTERPRISE AWARD WINNER 2026 
Photo Experience Ltd., based in Tullamore, was named 
the overall winner of the Offaly County Enterprise 
Award 2026 and will represent the county at the 
National Enterprise Awards in June. 
 
DISTRICT HEATING FEASIBILITY STUDY 
Contracts were signed between Offaly County Council and 
COWI (UK & Ire) for consultancy services to deliver a District 
Heating Feasibility Study within the Tullamore DZ.

PARK

Rhode Green Energy Park to SSE Renewables 
took place at Offaly County Council. SSE, a 
leading renewable energy developer, will 
develop an Operations Hub to support the nearby 
Yellow River Wind Farm, one of Ireland’s largest

SPACE

a successful tenderer for the redevelopment of 
33/34 JKL Street, the former Tesco Supermarket site, 
into a landmark town centre development.  
Following a competitive procurement process, Bretland Construction, based locally in 
Edenderry, has been identified as the successful tenderer.

ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND LOCAL ENTERPRISE OFFICE OFFALY 
PHOTO EXPERIENCE LTD. NAMED OFFALY ENTERPRISE AWARD WINNER 2026 
Photo Experience Ltd., based in Tullamore, was named the overall winner of the Offaly 
County Enterprise Award 2026 and will represent the county at the National Enterprise 
Awards in June. The company, 
founded in 2022, specialises in 
technology-driven photography 
systems for visitor attractions, 
combining hardware, software 
and operational expertise to 
deliver high-volume guest 
imaging solutions. In recognition of 
its strong growth and export 
potential, the business received a 
€2,500 prize. The National 
Enterprise Awards will take place 
on 18th June in The Mansion 
House, Dublin. Trophy designed by 
Offaly based craft maker Fiona 
Scott. 
 
A FOND FAREWELL AND BEST WISHES TO LISA MOLLOY 
We would like to extend our sincere congratulations and thanks to our colleague Lisa 
as she takes up the role of Head of Enterprise with Laois County Council.  
Lisa has been an incredible member of our team, and her passion and dedication to 
businesses in Offaly have always 
shone through. She has made a 
lasting impact not just on us as a 
team, but on the businesses she 
has supported during her time 
with LEO. While she will be 
greatly missed, we are excited to 
see her progress in this next 
chapter. We thank Lisa for her 
outstanding contributions to LEO 
Offaly and wish her every 
success. We also look forward to 
continued collaboration between 
our counties in the years ahead.

DRIVING EFFICIENCY: BUSINESS BREAKFAST WITH DECLAN LENAHAN 
A Business Breakfast event was held on 26 May, delivered by Declan Lenahan of DL 
Consultancy, focusing on driving 
productivity and cost efficiency 
for SMEs in a high-cost 
environment. With energy prices 
remaining elevated, the session 
highlighted practical supports 
available through LEO Offaly, 
including Lean for Business, 
Digital for Business and Green 
for Business. Attendees gained 
valuable insights, real-life 
examples and simple tools to 
help reduce costs, improve 
efficiency and operate more 
sustainably. 
 
 
LUNCH & LEARN – KILCORMAC 
LEO Offaly will host a Lunch & Learn session in Kilcormac Workwell Hub on Tuesday, 16 
June, providing local business owners with an overview of the key  
supports available to help them start, grow and scale their businesses. The session will 
give attendees the opportunity to engage directly with LEO staff, ask questions and 
network over a light lunch. This session will highlight how LEO Offaly can support 
businesses in the county to improve performance, enhance sustainability and achieve 
growth.

EURO-TOQUES AWARD RECOGNITION FOR GARRYHINCH WOOD EXOTIC 
MUSHROOMS 
Garryhinch Wood Exotic  
Mushrooms have been recognised 
at the 2026 Euro-Toques Ireland 
Food Awards, winning in the 
“Land” category for its innovative 
and sustainable mushroom 
cultivation. The awards celebrate 
excellence in Irish food production 
and highlight producers who 
demonstrate strong commitment 
to quality, sustainability and 
craftsmanship. This national 
recognition reflects the company’s 
continued growth and the strength 
of Offaly’s artisan food sector. 
 
BIASOL ACHIEVES INTERNATIONAL RECOGNITION AT WIMBLEDON 2026 
BiaSol has achieved a significant milestone, with its Oat Bites selected as a snack for the 
competitor area at Wimbledon 2026.  
 Founded by siblings Ruairi and Niamh Dooley, 
the Offaly based brand produces clean-label, 
high-fibre snacks using upcycled grains.  
This selection reflects the product’s strong 
nutritional profile and sustainability credentials, 
and represents a major international 
endorsement, with BiaSol products now 
helping to fuel elite athletes at one of the 
world’s most prestigious sporting events. 
 
NATIONAL MANUFACTURING & SUPPLY CHAIN CONFERENCE 2026 
We attended the National Manufacturing & Supply Chain Conference & Exhibition in the 
RDS, Dublin on 27–28 May 2026. The event provided valuable insights into key industry 
trends including digitalisation, automation and sustainability, while also offering strong 
networking opportunities. LEO Offaly client DTS Decontamination Technical Services 
exhibited at the event, showcasing their expertise and highlighting the strength of 
advanced manufacturing and technical services within the county.

DUBLIN TECH SUMMIT 2026 
LEO Offaly attended the Dublin Tech Summit, one of Europe’s leading technology 
conferences, bringing together global leaders in innovation, digital transformation and 
emerging technologies. The event provided valuable insights into trends such as AI, 
sustainability and scaling technology businesses, while also offering strong networking 
opportunities relevant to supporting the growth of Offaly-based enterprises. 
 
SSE RENEWABLES CONTRACT SIGNING – RHODE GREEN ENERGY PARK 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The contract signing for the sale of Site B at Rhode Green Energy Park to SSE 
Renewables took place at Offaly County Council. SSE, a leading renewable energy 
developer, will develop an Operations Hub to support the nearby Yellow River Wind 
Farm, one of Ireland’s largest onshore wind farms.  
This development marks a significant milestone for the park, establishing SSE as its first 
sustainable business and supporting future investment in the region. The project will 
also create local employment, with skilled technicians required to support the ongoing 
operation and maintenance of the wind farm.

TOURISM 
PRINT ADVERTS AND EDITORIAL  
‘Your Ireland’ magazine, a tourism supplement for the Celtic Media group, which 
includes the Offaly Independent newspaper was published in May.  The supplement is 
distributed within numerous newspaper titles and reaches counties Offaly, Westmeath, 
Meath, Cavan, Monaghan & Mayo.  Offaly tourism advertised in the supplement and 
secured advertorial space, focusing on promoting cycling for visitors to Offaly this 
Summer.  
                       
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
A wonderful article on Offaly was featured in The Spirit of Ireland Magazine in March.  
Targeting the North American market, the total distribution is 100,000 copies.  The 
magazine is available to all members of the North American Trade Association, 15,000 
Irish stores in the USA and Canada, USA Tourism Ireland Offices, the top 2,500 US tour 
operators that specialise in Ireland. An advert accompanied the editorial featuring an 
array of some of Offaly’s iconic attractions. 
 
NATIONAL RADIO CAMPAIGN 
A national radio campaign marketing Offaly as a destination was broadcast during April 
and May.  The adverts ran on stations throughout the country including, 2FM, Today FM, 
Red FM & Q Radio in Northern Ireland. The 20 second advert inspires the listeners to 
visit whilst reinforcing our new brand ‘Off we go!’

Offaly County Council Monthly Management Report                                                                      May 2026 
 
9 | P a g e  
 
SOCIAL MEDIA  
Two high profile celebrities visited Offaly in April/May showcasing their visit on social 
media; 
The much-loved TV presenter, artist and author Timmy Mallet cycled through Offaly in 
April, highlighting many attractions including Meelick Weir, Banagher Outdoor Pool and 
Birr Castle Demense. With over 184k followers on Facebook and 91k on Instagram, his 
stories and reel gained great interest from his wide audience. 
Instagrammer and GAA Podcaster Kevin Penrose spent 3 days in Offaly from 29th April 
to 1st May.  His action-packed itinerary, appealed to his younger demographic and his 
trip included water sports, Croghan Hill at sunset, cycling the Grand Canal Greenway, 
and sauna at Lough Boora Discovery Park.   
 
OFFALY TOURISM MARKETING AGM 
The 2025 AGM for Offaly Tourism Marketing (CLG) was held in Birr on 19th May.  Birr 
Castle Demesne hosted the meeting with was followed by a members meeting. Cllr.  
Eleanor Clendennen was voted in as the new Chairperson of Offaly Tourism Marketing 
with Donal Collins, BNM, the new vice chairperson.  Thereafter attendees were then 
treated to a tour of the wonderful interior of Birr Castle.  
 
JUST TRANSITION REGENERATIVE TOURISM SCHEME 
Dick’s Bike Hire officially launched their range of accessible bikes on 9th April. €148,000 
of funding support was received under the scheme to acquire the range of bikes.  
Conveniently located beside Ballycommon Bake House along the Grand Canal 
Greenway it will greatly enhance the offering for those wishing to experience the 
greenway.  
 
       
 
PHOTOGRAPHY  
Paul Moore will continue to capture imagery of the county and the Slieve Bloom area 
throughout the Spring/Summer.  Two projects funded under LEADER and ORIS have 
elements of photography. His work will enhance our image library, providing fresh 
seasonal content for use across social media and the website.

EU JT DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION PROGRAMME 
The redevelopment of www.visitoffaly.ie is progressing well, with the new website 
scheduled to launch in June 2026. The refreshed platform will feature a modern and 
vibrant design that reflects our new brand identity. It will showcase enhanced imagery 
and increased use of video to effectively highlight the diversity, character, and appeal 
of Offaly as a visitor destination. 
 
TULLAMORE SHOW 
Expressions of interest for exhibiting at the Experience Offaly Pavilion at the Tullamore 
Show, taking place in August, opened at the end of April and closed on 20th May. 
Demand was strong and the 30 exhibitors have now been selected.  Preparations are 
underway to ensure the pavilion’s continued success at this year’s show.

ROADS 
EMERGENCY PAVEMENT SCHEME – N52 BIRR (WOODFIELD) 
Offaly County Council has identified the N52 Birr EPARR scheme at Woodfield as a 
priority Emergency Pavement Scheme for 2026. A total allocation of €250,000 has been 
secured to deliver road surfacing improvements over approximately 700 metres of the 
N52 on the northern approach to Birr. 
Initial approval has been received from Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII) to proceed 
to tender for these Emergency Pavement Asset Renewal works. 
Tender documentation is currently being finalised, with invitations to tender expected 
to issue in June. Subject to TII Gateway 2 approval, it is anticipated that works will 
commence in late July. 
This targeted investment will improve pavement condition, enhance road user safety, 
and maintain the standard of this important national route. 
 
GEO AP FUNDING SCHEMES - €100K 
Offaly County Council has received approval for two GEOAP schemes on the Tullamore 
Bypass, located at Mucklagh and Arden, each with an allocation of €50,000.  These 
targeted interventions will support essential maintenance and protection works on the 
road network, addressing localised defects and helping to extend pavement life. The 
schemes form part of the ongoing programme to sustain network condition and 
enhance overall road safety across the county. 
 
ACTIVE TRAVEL 
Active Travel projects continue to progress across Offaly with funding provided by the 
National Transport Authority, supporting improved safety, accessibility, and sustainable 
travel options. 
At planning stage, Safe Routes to School scheme at Coláiste Íosagáin, Portarlington 
(R420) has been issued for public consultation, with submissions closing on 29th May. 
The project will consist of construction of new footpaths and controlled crossings to 
provide safe pedestrian links from Comhaltas Portarlington car park and & 
developments to Coláiste Íosagáin. The estimated project cost is €390,000. 
At construction stage, works are ongoing at Cox’s Bridge, Tullamore (€375,000), and at 
the three pedestrian crossings in Edenderry (€400,000). In addition, the Bus Stop 
Enhancement Programme is being delivered by Edenderry MD direct labour crews, 
with installations currently underway at Bracknagh, Clonbullogue and Portarlington.

14 | P a g e  
 
Notice of proposed Variation no. 1 of the Offaly County Development Plan 2021-2027 was 
published on 15th May.  The reason for the proposed variation is: 
 
(i) 
To provide increased housing growth requirements in alignment with the 
‘National Planning Framework Implementation: Housing Growth Requirement 
Guidelines’, published 29th July 2025, through the provision of additional ‘New 
Residential’ land use zonings. The proposed variation will provide for increased 
housing growth requirements which will extend beyond the lifetime of the 
current Development Plan i.e. up to 2030.  
(ii) 
Provision of ‘Open Space, Amenity and Recreation’ land use zoning on a site 
in Birr to reflect its established use as a sports and recreation ground. 
(iii) 
Provision of ‘Existing Residential’ land use zonings to provide for the rezoning 
of a site in Tullamore from ‘Enterprise and Employment’ zoning to ‘Existing 
Residential’ zoning and for the rezoning of lands from ‘Strategic Residential 
Reserve’ zoning to ‘Existing Residential’ zoning at Ferbane, reflecting their 
existing use as residential. 
(iv) 
Provision of ‘Business or Technology Park’ land use zoning of an identified 
strategic land bank in Tullamore to facilitate future economic development.  
(v) 
Provisions for ‘Peatland and Nature Corridors’ (Currently referred to as 
‘Wilderness Corridors’). The proposed Variation No. 1 proposes to update 
existing provisions on ‘Wilderness Corridors’, by way of amendments to 
objective BLO-28, Policy CAEP-38 and other associated text changes within the 
existing County Development Plan, in conjunction with mapping to give effect 
to ‘Peatland and Nature Corridors’ within the County. 
 
The proposed variation is available for public inspection online and at the Planning 
Office until 4pm Tuesday 16th June during which written submissions may be made to 
the planning authority either online or by hard copy.

AIR QUALITY – EDENDERRY CLEAN AIR INITIATIVE PILOT PROJECT 
Reﬂecting the on-going progress of the Edenderry Clean Air Initiative, Oﬀaly Co. Co. 
have been selected by the Department of Climate, Energy & Environment (DCEE) to 
work with consultants EnvEcon to develop a spatial proﬁle of Edenderry to inform a 
targeted residential retroﬁt programme. Targeting residential retroﬁt in areas of higher 
particulate emissions may reduce air quality and related health issues, essentially 
feeding into an Air Quality Roadmap. Oﬀaly Co. Co. are leading Nationally in the 
development of Air Quality Roadmaps in advance of the EU Air Quality Directive which 
will come into force in 2030. 
The consultancy project will conduct spatial proﬁling, assess the energy baseline, 
examine retroﬁt pathways and ultimate make recommends on strategic targeting. 
 
 
 
Oﬀaly County Council is also continuing in its work to better understand and improve air 
quality in Edenderry. The 2026 Air Quality Pilot Project builds on last year’s study by 
expanding the number of sensors, improving the type of data collected, and increasing 
public awareness about the importance of clean air.

WATER QUALITY 
The Water Quality Team hosted the Q2 Eastern & Midlands Regional Operational 
Committee meeting on 20th May.  This was attended by a range of stakeholders 
engaged in activities to advance the requirements of the Water Framework 
Directive.  The WQ Team gave a presentation providing the Oﬀaly perspective on the 
realities of implementing the roles assigned in the National RBMP.  As one of the smaller 
LAs in the region, the challenges of managing the statutory roles, while balancing the 
approach to improve water quality in speciﬁc catchments was examined.  Water quality 
trends in Oﬀaly are showing a greater decline rate than the national average – 16 
waterbodies declined and 5 improved in recent updates.   Focused works on selected 
waterbody catchments in Oﬀaly commenced in 2025, supported by additional scientiﬁc 
resources.

CLIMATE ACTION: 
Offaly County Council hosted CARO ASBS and five other local authorities for workshop 
4 of the Pilot LA Green Flag Trial.  Staff came together to agree a pilot application which 
will be used to determine the viability of a Green Flag programme for local authorities.  
Upon review and analysis of these applications, a report will be sent to the ECCE 
committee of the CCMA for discussion. 
 
As the Local Authority Climate Action Plan (LACAP) starts to enter its second cycle, 
Offaly County Council Climate Action Team members participated in the first workshop 
organised by CARO EM and supported by DCEE designed to reflect on the previous 
statutory LACAP Guidelines and provide comments on how the next iteration of these 
guidelines can be improved and adapted ahead of the 2029-2034 plan making process.

NEW WATER FOUNTAIN AT BALLINAGAR NATIONAL SCHOOL 
Oﬀaly County Council Climate Team members were invited to support Ballinagar Group 
Water Scheme and the National Federation launch their new water fountain at Ballinagar 
National School.  As a speciﬁc action within our LACAP to increase the number of water

ENERGY 
Mid-May saw the deadline for submission to the 
annual SEAI M&R energy reporting portal.  Oﬀaly 
County Council successfully submitted all our 
energy related data to SEAI ahead of time.  
We are conﬁdent of building on progress in against statutory legally binding targets 
which saw the organisation achieve 41.6% increase in Energy Eﬃciency and 40.9% 
reduction in total CO2 emissions in 2024 (against relevant baselines).  Provisional 2025 
results are expected to be published by SEAI in Q3 2026.

PATHFINDER PROJECTS 
Oﬀaly County Council hosted a ‘kick-oﬀ’ meeting for Stage 2a on our two Pathﬁnder 
projects (Áras an Chontae & Tullamore Leisure Centre as our towns highest energy using 
Signiﬁcant Energy Users SEU’s).  All parties involved i.e. OCC, MDDT, SEAI, EED & M&V 
consultants and RRA Project Management launched the next stage of the process 
which will see a detailed cost and energy templates developed for each building based 
on the measures selected from Stage 1.  Outputs will include a Stage 2a Report for 
review and approval before moving towards Stage 2b i.e. tender documentation 
preparation and publication. 
 
DISTRICT HEATING FEASIBILITY STUDY 
Contracts were signed between Offaly County Council and COWI (UK & Ire) for 
consultancy services to deliver a District Heating Feasibility Study within the 
Tullamore DZ.   
This study will align with SEAI DH Centre of Excellence guidance and will give specific 
attention to the potential of clean renewable geothermal heating, building on the 
previous ‘pre-feasibility study’, as a source for any possible DH network.  The study is 
100% funded from SEAI Pathfinder programme.

REGENERATION 
EDENDERRY COMMUNITY LIBRARY AND ARTS SPACE 
Offaly County Council announced the appointment of a successful tenderer for the 
redevelopment of 33/34 JKL Street, the former Tesco Supermarket site, into a landmark 
town centre development. Following a competitive procurement process, Bretland 
Construction, based locally in Edenderry, has been identified as the successful 
tenderer. A pre-contract meeting was held on Thursday, 30 April, and contract signing is 
expected in the coming weeks. A construction start date in early June has been agreed. 
A Rural Regeneration Development Fund (RRDF) of €12.2m was secured in 2024 by 
Offaly County Council for this development with match funding required from Offaly 
County Council of 20% from Offaly County Council’s own resources from both 
Development Contributions and Local Property Tax. 
The project will deliver a newly constructed Community Library and Arts Space, 
complemented by outdoor programming areas, along with a new pedestrian and cycle 
connection linking JKL Street to Blundell Avenue and the wider Blundell area. The 
scheme also includes site boundary works, enabling works, and significant public realm 
improvements, featuring biodiversity-focused landscaping, accessible parking, and the 
creation of a new urban plaza with seating.
